what_its_for: Oteseconazole is an antifungal medicine used to reduce the number of yeast infections (vaginal candidiasis) that keep coming back in women who are past their childbearing years (postmenopausal) or who cannot get pregnant. It is not used to treat an active yeast infection.
how_to_take: Take oteseconazole capsules by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or open them. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Your doctor will likely first prescribe a short course of fluconazole to clear your current infection before you start oteseconazole.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose and schedule. A common approach is: first, you may take fluconazole (a separate antifungal) for a few days to treat an active infection, then you start oteseconazole. A typical oteseconazole schedule is 600 mg (six 100 mg capsules) on Day 1, then 450 mg (four and a half 100 mg capsules) on Day 2, followed by 150 mg (one and a half 100 mg capsules) once weekly for 11 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose on the regularly scheduled day. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store oteseconazole at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container, away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not take oteseconazole if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or could become pregnant — this medicine can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid becoming pregnant during treatment and for at least one week after your last dose. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially fluconazole and other antifungals, since some combinations can affect how this medicine works. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual or severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); dark urine or very pale stools; or if your yeast infections do not seem to be improving or are getting worse. Also call if you think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Oteseconazole works by preventing yeast infections from coming back over time rather than treating an active infection right away. Most people begin to see fewer recurring yeast infections after completing the first few weeks of treatment. The full benefit is usually seen after completing the entire course of therapy. It may take several weeks before you notice a difference.
special_populations: This medicine is only approved for women who cannot get pregnant (postmenopausal women or those with a medical reason they cannot become pregnant). It should NEVER be used by women who are pregnant or who could become pregnant because it can cause serious birth defects. It is not approved for use in children. Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. If you are breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine.
